classes.observed_effect: The check caused the effect and measured the kernel or engine outcome. Conformance mode only.
classes.observed_state: Read back from the kernel, filesystem or engine without trusting configuration.
classes.configured: A setting that was requested and is recorded by the engine, but whose effect this check did not independently measure.
classes.unenforced: A known gap. Status is always gap; it is listed in every report that includes it and is never enforcement.

owners.lane1: live implementation via the backend's Engine API client (engine.*) and backend policy
owners.lane2: kernel, cgroup, filesystem and process observation (pkg/sandboxhost) and disposable-lab conformance

checks.what: /sys/fs/cgroup has the cgroup2 superblock magic and is the hierarchy root mount, not a bind of a subtree
lease slice cpu.max, memory.max and pids.max are finite
lease slice memory.swap.max is 0
engine slice memory.max and pids.max are finite
lease slice pids.max is finite and at least sandboxes x per-lease pids_max
the dedicated containerd and dockerd processes are in the engine slice
lease and engine slices are disjoint from the caller's own cgroup and every declared exclusive cgroup
the engine socket is the profile's root-only unix socket, not the default /var/run/docker.sock
engine server version equals the reviewed pin
engine data root is the profile path on the dedicated data filesystem
storage driver overlay2 (containerd snapshotter off) backed by xfs with d_type
engine reports systemd cgroup driver on cgroup v2
engine uses the dedicated containerd socket and namespaces, and that containerd's root is on the data filesystem
engine has no bridge network; only host and none exist
iptables, ip6tables, ip-forward and ip-masq are disabled in daemon configuration
engine default runtime is runsc
registered runsc path and arguments match the profile and the file hashes to the pinned sha256
daemon default log driver json-file with max-size and max-file
insecure registry CIDRs are only Docker's built-in loopback ranges, only docker.io is indexed, and no mirrors are configured
the dedicated engine holds no container without the backend's sandbox label
data filesystem is xfs with project quota accounting and enforcement on
data filesystem is its own finite mount whose size matches the profile
run root (sockets, exec-root, containerd state) is a size-limited tmpfs
profile aggregate CPU, memory, pids and disk are within the observed slice limits and data filesystem less reserves
image, layer and pull-temp bytes are shared, not charged to any lease, and bounded only by the data filesystem; a pull can make a lease hit ENOSPC below its own quota
containerd places shim sockets in the host-wide /run/containerd/s directory
only network mode none is provisioned; public and allowlist egress have no enforcement and must be refused
the engine gives image-declared volumes no per-lease quota; the backend must refuse images whose config declares Volumes
engine records runtime runsc, network none, the lease cgroup parent, CPU, memory, swap, pids, writable-layer size, bounded logs, no mounts, all caps dropped, no-new-privileges
the container PID executes the pinned gVisor sentry
the sentry's actual cgroup is a child of the lease slice
the sentry cgroup cpu.max, memory.max, memory.swap.max and pids.max equal the lease
every gVisor process of the instance is in the lease slice or the engine slice
host-side network namespace of the sentry has only lo and no route off lo
the sandbox's own /proc/net/dev lists only lo
no Docker or containerd socket path exists in the guest and the guest mount table names none
IPv4 metadata, IPv4 public and IPv6 public TCP attempts each fail with exactly the no-route line
53/udp to public IPv4 and IPv6 resolvers and a DNS lookup fail for lack of a route
ICMP echo (IPv4 and IPv6) from a network=none probe granted NET_RAW cannot leave the sandbox; evidence names whether runsc refused the socket or the send had no route
host listeners on 127.0.0.1 and the host primary address receive no connection; the sandbox's 127.0.0.1 is its own loopback
a rootfs write stops within 4 MiB of the writable-layer quota with ENOSPC or EDQUOT while the data filesystem has free space, and exactly one full XFS project matches
container log rotates to exactly max-file files within the cap, on the data filesystem
guest process creation stops at or below the lease pids limit
a /tmp write larger than the lease memory cannot complete; the failure is attributed to the lease memory limit
two leases whose own limits are not reached are stopped by the aggregate lease slice memory limit
a container started without an explicit cgroup parent or storage size still lands in the lease slice with the default writable-layer quota
negative control: an image-declared volume accepts writes beyond the writable-layer quota, proving lease.image_volumes_refused is necessary
after destroy, containers, volumes, images, sentry processes and child cgroups are gone
